newsitem.title: UK: Slovenia SKB 9-mo pretax profit $16.63 mln.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia SKB 9-mo pretax profit $16.63 mln.

text.p: Slovenia's second largest bank, SKB Banka dd made a pretax profit of $16.625 million in the first nine months of 1996 compared with $7.96 million for the whole of 1995, director Cvetka Selsek told a presentation in London.
"In order to strengthen its balance sheet, the bank intends to take all fourth quarter profits to reserves," she said.

The bank, which is also the second largest quoted company on the Ljubljana Stock Exchange, plans to undertake a global depositary receipt (GDR) offering in the first quarter of next year and obtain a listing on the London Stock Exchange.
Selsek said that the bank aimed to increase return on equity to 10-12 percent from 9.5 percent in the first nine months of this year and 4.1 percent in 1995.
"We are about to fulfil this goal next year," she said.
The bank also believes that it can expand within Slovenia as the domestic banking system comes under pressure.

"Slovenia is definitely overbanked and there will be a process of consolidation, especially among regional banks. We have made approaches in the past but our environment has not been adapted to bids although that will change with a new law," Selsek said.
SKB also aims to obtain a credit rating from Standard & Poors in 1997.
The bank is currently rated "BBB" by Thomson BankWatch.
SKB's Selsek believes that Nova Ljubljanska Bank, the country's largest which is currently state owned, will come to the stock market in 1997, although the state is likely to try to keep a stake.
